# Make Your Home Merry and Bright: Holiday Decorating Ideas to Try


Published On: October 16, 2026


•


3 min read


•


The holidays are a great time to make your home feel a little cozier, brighter and more festive. And you don’t need a house full of decorations to make a big impact.


Whether you love traditional decor, prefer a simple winter-inspired look or like to mix old favorites with new finds, a few thoughtful touches can transform the spaces you use every day.


**Megan Foster, the Interior Design Director for Cavco,** offers tips on making your home holiday ready. Megan leads the **Design Innovation Team at Cavco** , which develops curated home collections such as the[Studio Collection — where designer details come standard.](https://www.cavcohomes.com/studio-collection) (Read Megan’s decorating tips for Autumn in[Fall Home Décor Ideas](https://blog.cavcohomes.com/2025-fall-decor-design-ideas-manufactured-homes/) .)


From the front porch to the kitchen and living room, here are some **holiday decorating ideas for your manufactured home this season** .


## 1. Start By Decorating the Front Porch


“When you decorate for the winter seasons,” says Megan, “start with the front porch. A wreath, seasonal doormat, lanterns or a few potted evergreens can instantly give your entryway a festive feel. If you have a covered porch, add a small tree, garland or weather-resistant ornaments for even more holiday spirit.”


Megan says to choose decorations that complement your home’s exterior rather than competing with it. “A few well-placed pieces can go a long way,” she says.


**Make your front porch feel festive with these simple touches:**


- Hang a seasonal wreath or garland
- Layer in warm lighting with battery-operated candles and string lights
- Dress up the doorstep with a seasonal doormat


---


##


## 2. Once Inside, Use Cozy Textiles in Holiday Colors


“For many families,” says Megan, “the living room and kitchen are the heart of holiday gatherings. A very budget-friendly way to decorate AND make your space cozy is with textiles in holiday themes and colors.”


**Give your living room and kitchen a seasonal update by adding:**


- Seasonal throw pillows and plush blankets. Use flannels and sweatery fabrics. Mix and match plaids and solids. Megan says, “Round pillows and lumbar pillows are a trendy addition to oversized pillows.” Mix things up and bring on the coziness.
- A small tree, gingerbread houses or Hanukkah wreaths – whatever says “holiday” to you.
- Garlands, ornaments, menorahs, dreidels… Use favorite decorations that represent your family’s holiday spirit.
- Battery-operated candles and string lights.

## 3. Add Holiday Touches to Tables and Small Spaces


You don’t have to decorate every room to make your home feel festive. A few seasonal details on the dining table, kitchen island, coffee table or entryway console can bring holiday cheer to the spaces you use every day.


**Try these simple ways to decorate tables and countertops:**


- **Create a simple centerpiece.** Arrange greenery, ornaments or flowers in a bowl, tray or vase.
- **Set a festive table.** Use holiday napkins and colorful placemats.
- **Make use of vertical space.** Add a small wreath, seasonal artwork or a decorative wall hanging to bring holiday style to a bare wall.
